correctness.rationale: For every R≥1, reversal/complement classes exhaust binary target patterns of lengths m≤4. Each nonexceptional class has a uniform forcing word of length m+2R whose every m+R subsequence contains the target; constant/two-run, alternating-embedding, and second-zero arguments prove the three nontrivial cases. An explicit contradiction independently proves insertion covering for the two exceptional avoidance sets. The exact reduction from a missing deletion target to F_y, greedy extension for maximality, and binomial matched-prefix count complete the proof. Reproduced checks include all patterns for radii 1..5, independent brute deletion subsets for 1..3, templates for 1..50, family size and deletion-target checks for 1..7. Finite checks are corroboration, not universal proof.

originality.rationale: Xie–Sun–Ge (2026), Theorem III.2, constructs the 0110-avoidance insertion cover, but their Sections III.1–III.4 do not imply the necessity of n≥R+4 or the exhaustive statement that the two complement-related avoidance families are the only inclusion-maximal separators at first onset. This is a best-knowledge publication comparison, not a proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: The classification resolves the sharp first blocklength where insertion covering can fail to imply deletion covering for every error radius, and determines both and only both inclusion-maximal separating code families at that natural boundary. It converts a source existence example into a necessary and complete structural boundary, with one orbit under complement and a closed size formula, rather than computing an arbitrary small case or optimizing an unrelated parameter.
